frames.description: Back in the cellar. Nagoji chained in his place. Eyes closed. His hands are raw meat.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I closed my eyes. Not in prayer. In calculation.

frames.correction: Eyes naturally closed to match the scripted calculation beat; all composition and reserve geometry preserved.

frames.description: A grid of four small insets inside the panel, what he is counting: guards at the door, a key ring, boots on the stair, the bucket.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: How many guards. How often they changed. Which men wore keys and which carried only cudgels. How many steps from the stair to the courtyard.

frames.correction: Portuguese garrison guards in muted earth kit; preserved from accepted page 9 art pass.

frames.description: A whisper passing along the chained line, man to man, drawn as leaning heads in the dark.

copy.speaker: PRISONER
copy.text: They are gathering us for transport. South. By ship. For labour.

frames.correction: Changed only Nagoji's lower dhoti to dirty cream or ivory; upper tunic remains ochre and all reserve geometry is preserved.

frames.description: Full width. Nagoji's eyes opening in the dark.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Ships meant movement. Movement meant chances.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They had taken my name. They had tried to break my body.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They had forgotten the simplest lesson of the Deccan monsoon.

frames.correction: Accepted r2 close-up with one flush ear stud and no dangling ornaments.
